description.narrative:
Activity period: 2019-05-23 - 2024-03-31
Budget: 15 099 986 SEK
Partner: Centre pour la Gouvernance Démocratique (CGD)
Other donors: Denmark
The overall objective of the program was to contribute to strengthen the democracy and promote the good governance in Burkina Faso through the production of knowledge, the creation of spaces for dialogue and the questioning of actors of democratic governance. To achieve this overall objective, the project was structured in three (03) axes:
Axis 1: Strengthening constitutionalism, the rule of law and political and socio-economic governance; Axis 2: Promoting civic awareness, civility, social cohesion and good governance in the security sector; Axis 3: Institutional support and organizational strengthening of the CGD
No major amendements to the agreement were done during the agreement period.

The main results achieved by the programme are summarized as follows:
Axis 1 - Strengthening constitutionalism, the rule of law and political and socio-economic governance
1.1 Republican Institutions (electoral commission, judicial sector, the national assembly, political parties and territorial collectives) function in accordance with democratic standards, are credible and take into account gender
Under this objective, CGD has placed a heavy emphasis on the production of knowledge. Through annual reports on rule of law, the legislative work, diagonstics of elections and so on, the CGD has produced knowledge and insights which have been used to stimulate dialogue and influence the politics of the country. CGD has been involved, as a consultant, in the quasi-totality of legisliation passed in relation to governance, human rights and security. The mid-term evaluation indicated that 75 % of respondents found the studies and consultative work done by CGD to be highly relevant.
1.3 Republican Institutions are stable and the relationship between political actors is peaceful
In order to strengthen institutional stability and promote peaceful relations between political actors, the CGD initiated dialogue frameworks and organized celebrations of democracy. Democratic Dialogues, which consists of organizing public debates on topics of national interest with a view to improve democratic governance have, through the years, become a very important tool for democracy promotion in Burkina Faso, with 92 % of respondents in the mid-term evaluation confirming their importance. Almost 6000 individuals have directly participated in the democratic dialogues during the activity period.
1.4 Public Financial Management is improved and the rights of communities in extractive industries are known and applied
CGD contributed to budgetary transparency as well as the control and accountability of public institutions by organizing anti-corruption days, and launching advocacy campagins for the audit of the national assembly and the military. In relation to extractive industries, and in particular to increase the revenue that benefits the local communities, CGD has strengthened the capacity and knowledge of local community leaders as well as mining company about their respective rights and obligations. CGD has launched adovacy campagins highlihgting the environmental and social responsibility of mining companies. These activities have led to an increasing share of profits being re-invested locally, and has given local businesses access to the the procurement procedures of certain mining companies.
Axis 2 Promoting civic awareness, civility , social cohesion and good governance in the security sector
2.1 Actors and citizens have a responsible influence on public policy
CGD launched several initatives to strengthen the capacities of youth, journalists and CSOs in order to promote an inclusive and gender sensititve governance. CGD has trained young leaders in a wide-array of issues, such as political analysis, security policy, social cohesion and gender equality. In the same vein, student cells in thirteen universities were developed, each composed of a 100 students. This cells in turn strengthened the capacities of their members, organized conferences and advocacy campaigns, reaching a larger part of the burkinabé student population.
2.1 Social cohesion is strengthened for a durable peace
CGD produced several studies, notably one on national unity which was shared with the High Council for Reconciliation and National Unity (HCRUN) which let to the creation of a ministerial post for national reconciliation. In addition to studies and knowledge creation, the CGD organized a series of symposiums aimed at promoting civilo-military coordination and improve the relationship between citizens and the security forces (both the army and local security intiatives such as the Kogleweogo and Dozo militias).
Overall, 24 369 people, of whom 8 650 women, were directly touched by the activities of the CGD.
In relation to the agreed upon indicators used to monitor the success (or lack thereof) of the intervention, the following can be highlighted:
The indicator measuring institutional stability has gone from good to medium, mainly due to to two coup d'etats, as well as the increasing polarisation of society. All quantitative indicators (numbers of dialogues held etc.) have been reached, with the exception of the indicator measuring the number of difficulties resolved by the authorities as a result of democratic dialogues (13 issues resolved compared to the objective of 20).
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
